first_impression: This looks like a game someone cared about: the title, the evening cards and the warm low-poly valley have a cosy Short Hike meets Flock vibe, and the snow, mist and moonlit night evenings look great. My worry is that once I'm in the top-down herding camera, a lot of these 'different places' are the same olive-mustard lawn with tan paths, and the wolves barely show up in what I was shown.
best_things: The weather and time-of-day evenings give real visual range: the snowy pass with the black sheep standing out against white (evening-8-snow), the moonlit night watch with a red-ringed wolf creeping in (evening-5-night), and the clear circle Pip can see in the mist (evening-6-mist).

The season map (season-map, season-map-after-1) gives a proper reason to keep going: nine named evenings across summer to winter, stars out of 27, ribbons, charms bought with stars, best scores and a daily 'Friday's Evening'.

Each evening card teaches exactly one new twist in plain words (lambs that follow their mothers, Old Angus who has to be stared down, thunder that scatters the flock, a points-judged sheepdog trial), and the HUD always tells me what I need: home count, target, star goals, time to nightfall and time until the wolves.

worst_problems.problem: From the herding camera most locations look like the same flat olive or mustard lawn with tan dirt paths. Loch Ailsa, Crannach Corrie and the Glenbrae show field don't feel like new places: the loch and the crags only show up on the minimap, and Old Angus's corrie is one big mustard-yellow wash.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give each place its own ground: shingle and reeds along the loch edge, scree and boulders in the corrie, mown stripes, bunting and a crowd at the show field, heather on the moor. Let me see the landmark the card talks about in the play view.

worst_problems.problem: The low side-on shots during evening 1 hide the action. Two huge dark pines fill the middle of the screen, the wolf the shot is supposedly about is nowhere to be seen (only a red edge marker), and in the previous frame the wolf icon sits on top of a sheep. I can't tell if this is a cutscene or if I'm meant to be playing from it, since the HUD is still up.
worst_problems.suggestion: If it's a cinematic, hide the HUD, keep trees out of the foreground and actually frame the wolf coming out of the pines. If it's playable, it needs to show the threat, not a tree trunk.

worst_problems.problem: A dark rectangular slab cuts across the stream with a blocky blue chunk past it. It looks like a missing bridge or a rendering bug, and it sits right next to the victory card.
worst_problems.suggestion: Fix or replace whatever that slab is (a proper bridge or ford model) so the win screen doesn't look broken.

worst_problems.problem: Important things end up under the HUD. In the storm the stray sheep are behind the timer panel at the very top while Pip runs around an empty field of rain streaks. At night the flock sits on top of the 'A wolf is stalking your flock!' banner, which is half see-through and hard to read.
worst_problems.suggestion: Keep the camera framing sheep away from the top panels, and make warning banners solid or move them clear of the flock.

worst_problems.problem: The trial field is washed out with soft vertical light stripes that look like smudges on the screen, and the gates are just thin white posts that almost vanish into the yellow grass. For a precision event I can barely see what I'm aiming at.
worst_problems.suggestion: Put coloured flags or painted gate frames on the trial gates, show a faint line through the next gate, and tone down the light shafts on that field.

boredom_points: Evening 1 was finished with 3:59 of daylight left out of about 4:50 (evening-1-result), with the wolves out for maybe 20 seconds. If the early evenings are this quick, the sunset-and-wolves tension from the store blurb never really happens.
Looking down at the same olive lawn from the same high angle in most evenings: by the third or fourth one the levels would blur together unless the twist on the card is strong.
Night Watch: guarding a tight bunch of 12 sheep for about four minutes waiting for dawn could drag. The result card says 0 lost and 0 rescued, so the wolves may not push hard enough to keep me busy.
Replaying the trial over and over on a plain flat field with no wolves just to go from 70 to 85 points.
confusions: What 'Flank Z X' in the bottom bar does: it's not in the title-screen key hints or on any evening card I saw.
Whether the low camera in e1-low-view and e1-wolf is a cutscene or gameplay, and why the wolf marker sits on top of a sheep.
At night the round white blobs scattered around Pip (evening-5-night) look exactly like lone sheep from above, but the counter says all 12 are safe, so I guess they are rocks?
The 1 to 9 row on the result cards shows three faint stars under every evening, so I can't tell which evenings I've actually earned stars on.
The trial counter starts at 100 points and presumably only goes down, which wasn't obvious until I read the card; 'Cross' being outlined in orange read like a warning rather than 'next gate'.
On the lambing evening I couldn't pick out which ones were lambs or where the lost lamb was at that zoom.
The dark slab across the stream in the Night Watch dawn shots: bridge, dam or bug?
wish_list: A clearly different look per place from the herding camera (loch shore, rocky corrie, heather moor, a show field with a crowd and judges' tent).
Charms that change how I play rather than +8% speed or 30% less stamina drain.
A leaderboard or friend scores for the daily evening, so the 'today' card has a real pull.
A free-herd sandbox or endless mode once the season is done, and a photo mode for those low golden-hour views.
A second dog to work with in the later evenings, or local co-op with two collies.
A little customisation for Pip (collar colour, name) earned through ribbons.
one_line_review: A warm, good-looking herding game with a real season to work through and lovely snow, mist and night evenings, held back by fields that too often look like the same mustard lawn from above.
